title: Delimiter-mixing in multi-function responses causing JSON parse failures (customer escalation)
creator: Maya Patel
description: Customer (ACME Corp) reported production errors where agent workflows that invoked multiple functions returned concatenated outputs that could not be parsed as valid JSON. Failures occurred across Hosted and Dedicated deployments and one Private deployment in the customer's VPC. Symptoms include partial JSON objects followed by a raw text delimiter ("---END TOOL---") and an extra newline, which breaks downstream structured-output parsers in customer code. The issue appears when two or more tool/function calls return outputs using different delimiter conventions and when streaming responses interleave boundary tokens with KV-cache entries.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use the agent chaining sample with two functions: invoice_extractor() and risk_scorer().
2) Enable streaming responses and structured_output mode, and send a request that triggers both functions in rapid succession.

3) Observe produced event stream: function A ends with a custom delimiter, function B starts immediately; in some runs the runtime emits both the delimiter and a KV cache flush marker on the same frame.
4) Attempts to JSON.parse the assembled payload in the client fail with 'Unexpected token - in JSON at position X'.
investigation_notes: 11/02: Oncall triage (Maya) — customer provided logs and sample transcript. Reproducible on dev with stress harness. Logged as P0 due to customer production impact.
11/03: Core runtime team (Ethan) bisected to streaming frame assembly layer; intermittent when continuous batching and prefix-KV cache flush co-occur.

11/04: Observed two root causes: (A) inconsistent delimiter normalization between older tool adapters and new structured-output framing; (B) race in streaming frame concatenation that sometimes omitted separator escaping when KV-cache metadata was present.
11/05: Confirmed affects Hosted/Dedicated runtimes and a private deployment where customer had an older tool-adapter plugin installed. Not a customer-side parsing bug alone.
11/06: Prioritization discussion: immediate mitigation + full fix. Agreed to backport fix to runtime-1.24 and cut emergency patch for Dedicated customers.
mitigation_actions: Short term: Server-side normalization of tool boundaries — insert strict JSON-safe separators and escape any raw delimiters before emitting a frame.
Customer guidance: Patch client-side parsers to ignore lines that match legacy delimiter patterns and to fall back to streaming-reassembly heuristics (support ticket sent with recommended regex).
Ops: Notify Dedicated customers with active canaries and schedule emergency patch deployment windows.
proposed_fix: 1) Normalize delimiter tokens at the source adapter layer: canonicalize all tool terminators to '\u001E' (RS record separator) and ensure it's JSON-escaped when included in text outputs.
2) Add an atomic frame-assembly check to the streaming aggregator that verifies frame boundaries when KV-cache flush markers are present.
3) Add end-to-end tests in the runtime harness simulating mixed-adapter outputs and streaming interleaving under high-concurrency.
4) Backport to runtime-1.24 and schedule a hotfix branch 'hotfix/1.24.3-delimiter-normalization'.
rollout_plan: Canary on Hosted region us-west-2 for 2 hours with synthetic agent scenarios (target error rate <0.01%).

Dedicated: notify top 10 impacted tenants and schedule rolling upgrade windows in their reserved pools. Automatic fallback to prior parser-enabled model variant during rollout if errors exceed threshold.
Private: provide customer-specific patch bundle and support runbook; coordinate with Solutions Eng (Luca) for on-prem installs.
qa_notes: QA to validate with three permutations: (A) single tool streaming, (B) back-to-back tool calls with different delimiters, (C) stress with KV-cache flush on high-concurrency.
Add fuzz test that injects random ASCII delimiter sequences into function outputs to ensure normalization works.
Manual verification: replay the original customer's failing transcript after hotfix applied.
comments: 11/02 Maya: Filed after phone call with ACME SRE — they saw cascading failures in downstream microservices that expect strict JSON from tool outputs.
11/03 Ethan: Identified candidate patch; will instrument streaming aggregator to capture raw frames for 24h to gather more samples.
11/04 Priya (PM): Prioritize hotfix for Hosted and Dedicated. Coordinate comms and status page updates. Inform support to offer rollbacks if customers request.
11/05 Luca (Solutions Eng): One Private customer on older adapter; will coordinate bundle application with their infra team on 11/09.
11/06 Security (Anna): Reviewed patch surface area; no secrets handling changes. Security signoff not required for this patch.
11/07 QA (Diego): Added three new end-to-end tests and a fuzz harness; observed no regressions in unrelated structured-output flows.
11/08 Ethan: Deployed canary to us-west-2 — initial metrics show error rate dropped from 0.8% to 0.02% on synthetic tests. Preparing backport PR for dedicated clusters.
resolution: Partial mitigation deployed to Hosted canary. Full hotfix branch created and scheduled for backport to runtime-1.24 and Dedicated clusters. Private customer given patch bundle and on-call deployment support scheduled 2025-11-09. Postmortem to follow once Dedicated rollback window completes.
